issue_context.title: sidecar container readniess result to be used in Pod ready state also for pod.spec.restartPolicy = Never or OnFailure
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

I created a pod with sidecar container with following manifest:
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: simple-webapp
  labels:
    app: webapp
spec:
  tolerations:
  - key: "key1"
    operator: "Exists"
    effect: "NoSchedule"
  initContainers:
    - name: init-service
      image:  busybox
      command:
        - sleep
        - 5s
    - name: sidecar
      image:  busybox
      command:
        - sleep
        - 30s
      volumeMounts:
        - name: shared-logs
          mountPath: /var/log/nginx
      readinessProbe:
        exec:
          command:
          - cat
        initialDelaySeconds: 5
        periodSeconds: 5
      imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
      restartPolicy: Always
  containers:
  - name: main-application
    image: nginx
    volumeMounts:
      - name: shared-logs
        mountPath: /var/log/nginx
    resources:
      requests:
        memory: "100Mi"
        cpu: "0.5"
  volumes:
    - name: shared-logs
      emptyDir: {}
  restartPolicy: Never

```

watch the pod readiness. 
```
#before the sidecar container be restarted , the readiness is 2/2
watch kubectl  get pod
Every 2.0s: kubectl get pod                                                     

NAME                    READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
simple-webapp           2/2     Running   0          36s

#after the sidecar container be restarted, the pod readiness is 1/2, sidecar readiness result is not be used to the pod. 
NAME                    READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
simple-webapp           1/2     Running   2          2m15s

```
in [Sidecar containers and Pod lifecycle](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/sidecar-containers/#sidecar-containers-and-pod-lifecycle), it's mentioned "If a readinessProbe is specified for this init container, its result will be used to determine the ready state of the Pod."

it's true only for pod.spec.restartPolicy = Always, sidecar container readniess result will be used in Pod ready state, neither "Never" or "OnFailure".

I tested with v1.29.0

### What did you expect to happen?

I expect "If a readinessProbe is specified for this init container, its result will be used to determine the ready state of the Pod." also applicable to  pod.spec.restartPolicy = "Never" or "OnFailure".

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Set pod.spec.restartPolicy = "Never" or "OnFailure".

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

for pod \"default\"/\"simple-webapp-never\": Pod \"simple-webapp-never\" is invalid: status.initContainerStatuses[1].state: Forbidden: may not be transitioned to non-terminated state"

After a quick debug, it seems that the problem is the apiserver who is preventing the initContainerStatus from being changed from terminated to non-terminated state.

created a PR to address this.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/123323
Just a small comment on whether we need a cherry pick. This only affects specific pods with the new beta feature enabled. I don't think it is justifiable to cherry-pick this

@howardjohn do you think this bug is critical enough to cherry-pick.

Just discussed on sidecar WG and it feels that impact may be more dangerous than I undertsood. @gjkim42 will summarize
IIUC it doesn't seem that critical to Istio, epsecially if its high risk to backport
the fix is relatively easy, but I am operating from the assumption that everything is high risk to backport =)

I confirmed that the bug is not only limited to the sidecar container with `readinessProbe`. Kubernetes cannot update the terminated sidecar container' statuses from Job without the bugfix (regardless of the `readinessProbe`).

The sidecar container can continually restart but its container status will be stuck in the first terminated state. It seems like a quite critical bug for me.

review_comments: should we also check the feature gate here? what happens if the feature is disabled after the pod was created?

I think we shouldn't.

> what happens if the feature is disabled after the pod was created?

It ends up breaking the existing pods having sidecar containers if we check the feature gate here.
well, we do check the feature gate in other places?

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/109491f3cbaefcaf95e9e94ea0c216bfc38d6570/pkg/api/pod/util.go#L589-L595

Yes, the apiserver drops container.restartPolicy field if the FG is disabled AND the existing pod has no sidecar.
apiserver should allows the update requests for the existing sidecar container.

To be clear, if the container.restartPolicy is not nil (not dropped) here, it means that the feature gate is enabled or this request is updating the existing sidecar container which should be allowed.

We don't usually want to check gates except at "admission", or else we allow data in and then fail updates.  That said, I would drop a comment here with the gate name so that when we eventually remove the gate, we can grep for it and find this and remove the nil check.
